column1: # Real commands dispatched planwright workers ran, with the decision the
# deployed guard must reach for each. Rows are <expect><TAB><command>;
# expect is `allow` (the worker must never stall on this) or `defer`.
# Grow this file from live stalls: when a worker blocks on a command that
# should have been approved, add the verbatim command here as an `allow` row
# BEFORE fixing the guard, so the corpus proves the fix and pins it.
# @@PLUGIN_ROOT@@ and @@REPO_ROOT@@ are substituted by the harness with the
# test. Never write a literal path here: the guard only trusts an
# `R=<root>` assignment when that exact directory exists, so a literal one
# ties the row to one machine and one plugin version, and fails CI.
# Provenance of the 2026-09-14 rows: two tower-comms workers (tasks 2 and 3)
# stalled on their first tool call under plugin 0.41.1, which made unattended
# fleet dispatch impossible. Both commands are reproduced verbatim below.

column2: grep -n '^## \|^### ' specs/tower-comms/test-spec.md | head -40; for r in A1.1 A1.2 A1.3; do echo "=== $r"; awk -v r="REQ-$r" 'index($0,"**"r"**")||index($0,"### "r)||index($0,"- "r" ")||index($0,"**"r)==1{p=1;print;next} p&&/^- \*\*REQ-|^### REQ-|^## /{p=0} p{print}' specs/tower-comms/test-spec.md; done

env | grep -i 'planwright\|PLUGIN' ; echo ---; R=@@PLUGIN_ROOT@@; diff -rq $R/scripts scripts | head; echo "--- dispatch-fetch"; $R/scripts/dispatch-fetch.sh --spec specs/tower-comms @@REPO_ROOT@@; echo "exit $?"

column1: # --- awk: read-only programs the blanket `|` / `>` screens over-defer ---
# --- environment inspection (read-only; `env VAR=x cmd` is NOT) ---------

column2: while read l; do echo "$l"; done < f

column1: # --- regression baseline: already allowed, must stay allowed -----------

column2: for r in A B; do echo "=== $r"; awk -v r="REQ-$r" '{print}' f; done
if [ -f f ]; then cat f; fi

column1: # --- the four bypasses the 2026-09-14 lexer allowed (arbitrary exec / write)
# Each was verified to really run under mawk before the rewrite: the first
# three printed a uid, the fourth created the file. They defer now because an
# unplaceable `/` is rejected outright rather than scanned as code.
# --- two more the rewrite's own first draft allowed, caught before it shipped

column2: awk 'BEGIN{c="sh";s="id"} {x = "&" /2; print s | c; y=1/2}' f

column1: # --- brackets are allowed only where the program carries no vector at all
# --- guard_read used to collide with the hook's own locals, so the commonest
# loop variable in shell stalled every worker that wrote one

column2: while read i; do echo "$i"; done < f

column1: # --- flag screens used to match attached VALUES, not just flags
# --- jq reads the environment through program text, like awk's ENVIRON
# --- must NEVER be allowed: the guard is allow-only and fail-closed ----

column2: awk 'BEGIN{"id" | getline x; print x}' f
